_source.description: Major global selenium production and refining sites — byproduct of copper refining from anode slimes
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/); Selenium-Tellurium Development Association (STDA, https://www.stda.org/); Aurubis AG annual reports (https://www.aurubis.com/); JXTG/Eneos Holdings integrated reports; Umicore annual reports; Boliden AB annual reports; Pan Pacific Copper, Sumitomo Metal Mining, Mitsubishi Materials corporate publications; Jiangxi Copper, Tongling Nonferrous corporate reports; LS-Nikko Copper annual reports
_source.license: USGS: public domain; STDA: public summary data; company data: fair use summary
_source.notes: Selenium is produced almost exclusively as a byproduct of electrolytic copper refining, recovered from anode slimes during electrorefining. Global production estimated at ~3,500 tonnes/year (USGS). China (~25%), Japan (~15%), Germany (~10%), Belgium, Chile, and Russia are leading producers. Primary uses: CdTe thin-film solar cells (First Solar), glass decolorization/coloring, metallurgy (free-machining steels/alloys), electronics (photoreceptors), and chemicals. Designated a USGS critical mineral. Coordinates from USGS MRDS, company filings, and satellite verification. Capacity figures are estimates; exact selenium output by facility is often not publicly reported as it is a minor byproduct.

sites.name: Jiangxi Copper (Guixi Smelter)
sites.ownership: Jiangxi Copper (SSE: 600362; Jiangxi provincial state majority)
sites.notes: Guixi, Jiangxi Province. China's largest copper smelter/refinery complex (~1.5M tpa refined copper). Selenium recovered from anode slimes in electrolytic refinery. Major source of Chinese selenium production.

sites.name: Tongling Nonferrous Metals (Jinchang Smelter)
sites.ownership: Tongling Nonferrous (SZE: 000630; Anhui provincial state majority)
sites.notes: Tongling, Anhui Province. Major Chinese copper smelter with selenium recovery from anode slimes. Integrated smelting-refining complex.

sites.name: Daye Nonferrous Metals (Huangshi Smelter)
sites.ownership: China Nonferrous Metal Mining Group (CNMC, Chinese state-owned)
sites.notes: Huangshi/Daye, Hubei Province. Historic copper smelting region. Selenium recovered as byproduct of copper electrorefining from anode slimes.

sites.name: Yunnan Copper (Kunming Smelter)
sites.notes: Kunming, Yunnan Province. Major Chinese copper refinery with precious metals and selenium/tellurium recovery. Part of Chinalco group.

sites.name: JXTG/Eneos Saganoseki Smelter
sites.notes: Saganoseki, Oita Prefecture, Kyushu. One of Japan's largest copper smelters (~450k tpa copper). Selenium and tellurium recovered from anode slimes in the electrolytic refinery. Major Japanese selenium source.

sites.name: Mitsubishi Materials (Naoshima Smelter & Refinery)
sites.notes: Naoshima Island, Kagawa Prefecture (Seto Inland Sea). Continuous copper smelting (Mitsubishi Process) with electrolytic refinery. Selenium recovered from precious metals refinery treating anode slimes.

sites.name: Pan Pacific Copper (Onahama Smelter)
sites.notes: Onahama (Iwaki), Fukushima Prefecture. Flash smelting copper operation with electrolytic refinery. Selenium and tellurium recovered from anode slimes. Resumed operations after 2011 earthquake/tsunami damage.

sites.name: Sumitomo Metal Mining (Niihama/Toyo Smelter)
sites.notes: Toyo Smelter & Refinery, Niihama, Ehime Prefecture. Integrated copper-nickel smelting complex. Selenium recovered from copper anode slimes in electrolytic refinery.

sites.name: Aurubis Hamburg
sites.ownership: Aurubis AG (ETR: NDA; Salzgitter AG is largest shareholder)
sites.notes: Hamburg-Veddel. Europe's largest copper refinery (~450k tpa cathode copper). Major global selenium producer from anode slimes processing. Aurubis is one of the world's largest selenium producers. Also significant tellurium source.

sites.name: Aurubis Lunen
sites.notes: Lunen, North Rhine-Westphalia. Aurubis secondary copper smelter processing recycled copper and complex materials. Selenium recovered from recycling process. Complement to Hamburg primary refinery.

sites.name: Umicore Precious Metals Refining (Hoboken)
sites.notes: Hoboken, Antwerp. One of the world's largest precious metals and specialty metals refineries. Processes copper anode slimes and complex recyclables. Major European selenium and tellurium producer. Treats ~350k tonnes of complex feed materials annually.

sites.name: Metallo (Aurubis Beerse)
sites.notes: Beerse, Antwerp Province. Secondary copper smelter focused on recycling complex copper-bearing materials. Selenium recovered from processing residues. Acquired by Aurubis from Metallo Group in 2020.

sites.name: Codelco Chuquicamata Refinery
sites.notes: Chuquicamata, Antofagasta Region, Atacama Desert. One of the world's largest open-pit copper mines with integrated refinery. Selenium recovered from anode slimes. Chile is a significant selenium producer due to massive copper refining volumes.

sites.name: Enami Ventanas Refinery
sites.notes: Ventanas, Valparaiso Region. State-owned custom copper smelter/refinery processing concentrates from small/medium Chilean miners. Selenium recovered from anode slimes. Environmental concerns over emissions in Puchuncavi-Quintero industrial zone.

sites.name: Asarco Amarillo Copper Refinery
sites.notes: Amarillo, Texas. US copper electrolytic refinery (~230k tpa cathode). Selenium recovered from anode slimes in precious metals plant. One of few remaining US primary copper refineries.

sites.name: Freeport-McMoRan Miami Smelter
sites.notes: Miami, Gila County, Arizona. Copper smelter processing concentrates from Freeport's Arizona mines (Morenci, Bagdad, Safford). Selenium recovered from smelter/refinery byproducts. Anode slimes sent to Asarco or processed on-site.

sites.name: Norilsk Nickel (Norilsk/Krasnoyarsk)
sites.notes: Norilsk, Krasnoyarsk Krai (Arctic Siberia). World's largest nickel-copper-PGM producer. Selenium recovered from copper refining anode slimes at the Nadezhda smelter and copper electrolysis plant. Significant global selenium source.

sites.name: UMMC Copper Refinery (Verkhnyaya Pyshma)
sites.notes: Verkhnyaya Pyshma, near Yekaterinburg, Sverdlovsk Oblast. UMMC's main copper electrolytic refinery. Selenium recovered from anode slimes processing. One of Russia's largest non-Nornickel copper producers.

sites.name: Boliden Ronnskar Smelter
sites.notes: Ronnskar, Skelleftea, Vasterbotten County. Integrated copper smelter processing primary concentrates and electronic scrap (one of world's largest e-waste recyclers). Selenium recovered from anode slimes and complex recycling residues.

sites.name: Boliden Harjavalta Smelter
sites.notes: Harjavalta, Satakunta region. Integrated copper and nickel smelter/refinery. Selenium recovered from copper electrolysis anode slimes. Processes concentrates from Boliden's Nordic mines and third-party material.

sites.name: Teck Trail Operations
sites.ownership: Teck Resources (TSX: TECK.B; recently sold coal business to Glencore)
sites.notes: Trail, British Columbia. One of the world's largest integrated zinc-lead smelting complexes. Selenium recovered from various metallurgical residues and byproduct streams. Also produces indium, germanium, and other specialty metals.

sites.name: LS-Nikko Copper Refinery (Onsan)
sites.ownership: LS Corp (51%), JX Nippon Mining & Metals (49%)
sites.notes: Onsan National Industrial Complex, Ulsan. South Korea's largest copper refinery (~700k tpa cathode copper). Selenium recovered from anode slimes in precious metals recovery circuit. Major Asian selenium source outside China/Japan.
